title: Markets, Orders and Prices
summary: How markets set prices, how orders work and what trading costs. Education only, not advice.

modules.title: What a Market Does and Who Trades in It
modules.subject: Markets and participants
modules.learned: Explain what a market does and name the main participants and their goals.

check.q: A cafe owner asks whether a broker that guarantees returns is safe. What is the right answer?
options: Yes, if the broker is popular
No. Guaranteed returns are a warning sign, and the licence and terms must be checked first
Yes, if a friend has used it
It depends only on the advertised return
check.explanation: Guaranteed returns are a warning sign. Checking the licence and terms is the first step.

modules.title: How Prices Form: Supply, Demand and the Spread
modules.subject: Prices and quotes
modules.learned: Read a two-way quote and explain how supply and demand set the price.

check.q: A quote shows a bid of 10.00 and an ask of 10.05. You buy at the ask and sell at once at the bid. What did you lose?
options: Nothing
0.05 per unit, the spread
10.00 per unit
0.10 per unit
check.explanation: Buying at the ask and selling at the bid loses the spread, here 0.05 per unit before any other costs.

modules.title: Order Types: Market, Limit and Stop
modules.subject: Orders
modules.learned: Choose between market, limit and stop orders and check an order before sending it.

check.q: A trader sets a stop below a buy price, and a fast market gaps through it. What is the likely fill?
options: Exactly at the stop
At the first available price, which may be well below the stop
Above the buy price
The order cancels itself
check.explanation: Once triggered, a stop becomes a market order. It fills at the available price, which can be far below the stop.

modules.title: Trading Costs and Execution Quality
modules.subject: Costs
modules.learned: Estimate the total cost of a trade and compare brokers on that total.

check.q: Two brokers: one has no commission but a wider spread, the other a tighter spread plus a commission. Which comparison is right?
options: Compare the spreads only
Compare the total cost of the same planned trade
Choose the one with the nicest website
Choose whichever spread looks smaller
check.explanation: Only the total cost of the same planned trade shows which broker is cheaper for your use.

modules.title: Candles, Timeframes and Chart Limits
modules.subject: Chart basics
modules.learned: Read a candle and a trend, and explain why charts describe the past rather than predict the future.

check.q: A trader changes the chart timeframe after a losing trade until the pattern looks clear. What is this an example of?
options: Good analysis
Hindsight bias
Risk management
Diversification
check.explanation: Changing the timeframe until a pattern appears is hindsight. It makes past charts look more predictive than they were.

modules.title: Why Markets Move: News, Liquidity and Gaps
modules.subject: Events and risk
modules.learned: Plan a response to scheduled news and explain how gaps and low liquidity affect orders.

check.q: News is due at 10:00 and a trader holds a position without a plan. What is the best next step?
options: Add to the position at 10:00
Decide in advance whether to hold through the release, and size the position to survive a bad fill
Trade the headline when it appears
Ignore the release because it is scheduled
check.explanation: A plan made before the release, with a size you can survive, protects against surprise and gaps.

questions.q: A small grocery in Huambo buys fuel every month and wants to fix next year's cost in advance. Which participant does it most resemble?
options: A speculator betting on price moves
A hedger reducing a risk it already carries
A market maker quoting both prices
A long-term investor in shares

questions.q: A friend promises that a broker will make you steady profits every month. What should you do first?
options: Deposit a small amount to test it
Check the broker's licence and treat the promise as a warning sign
Ask the friend to trade for you
Borrow money to deposit a larger amount

questions.q: What is the main difference between investing and trading?
options: Investing uses borrowed money and trading does not
Investing usually has a long time horizon, while trading involves more frequent buying and selling
Trading is always safer than investing
Investing only applies to currencies

questions.q: Why should a beginner use a demo account before a live account?
options: Demo accounts guarantee profits
Demo accounts allow practice and review without risking real money, although real money can change behaviour
Demo accounts remove all costs
Demo accounts use real money at fake prices

questions.q: Before depositing money, what should a careful beginner check about a broker?
options: Whether it advertises the highest returns
Whether it is licensed, how client money is held and what it charges
Whether its website has many photos
Whether a friend trades with it

questions.q: A quote shows a bid of 75.10 and an ask of 75.30. What is the spread?
Many buyers appear suddenly and few sellers are available. What is the most likely short-term effect on the price?
options: It tends to rise as buyers compete
It tends to fall
It stays exactly the same
It falls to zero

questions.q: A price moves after an unconfirmed rumour. Which statement is most accurate?
options: The rumour is proven true, because the price moved
Price can move on expectation alone, so the move does not prove the rumour
The move shows the true value of the asset
The market is always right, so the move must be correct

questions.q: A quiet market has a wide spread. What is the most sensible response for a careful trader?
options: Trade immediately to avoid missing a move
Wait for normal trading conditions and check the spread before placing an order
Double the position size
Ignore spreads because they do not matter

questions.q: Why is a price best described as information rather than a verdict on value?
options: Because prices are always fair
Because a price records the most recent agreement, which can differ from true value
Because prices never change
Because only professionals set prices

questions.q: You want to buy only if the price falls to a level you choose, and you will not pay more. Which order fits?
options: A market order
A buy limit order at that level
A sell stop order
A market order placed in the evening

questions.q: A limit order is placed and the price never reaches it. What happens?
options: The order fills at the nearest price
The order stays open and does not fill, so no trade happens
The broker cancels it automatically
The order fills at the next day's opening price

questions.q: Why can a stop order fill far from its stop price in a fast market?
options: Brokers add a fixed margin to stop orders
Once triggered, it becomes a market order, which fills at the best available price
Stop orders expire early
Stop orders only work overnight

questions.q: A trader wants speed and does not mind a small difference in price. Which order matches this goal?
options: A limit order far from the market
A market order
A stop-limit order
A sell limit order

questions.q: Before sending an order, what is the most useful check?
options: Assume the last order was right
Confirm the instrument, direction, size and price or stop
Send it quickly to beat the market
Check only the price

questions.q: A trade has a spread of 0.20, a commission of 0.05 per unit and expected slippage of 0.10 per unit. What is the total estimated cost per unit?
One broker has a narrow spread but charges commission on every trade. Another has a slightly wider spread and no commission. What should you compare?
options: Only the spread
The total cost of the same planned trade, including all fees
Only the broker's logo
Only the broker's marketing

questions.q: Your account is in one currency and you trade an asset priced in another. What cost should you watch?
options: Nothing, conversion is always free
The conversion margin each time money moves between currencies
Only the spread
Only the withdrawal fee

questions.q: What is slippage?
options: The fee charged by the regulator
The gap between the expected price and the price at which an order fills
The interest paid on deposits
The number of trades placed per day

questions.q: Why does execution quality matter to the price you pay?
options: It does not, only the spread matters
Slow fills, rejections and requotes change the price you actually receive
Execution only matters to professional traders
Execution affects only the broker's profit

questions.q: On a chart, a candle's close is above its open. What does this mean?
options: The price fell over the period
The price closed higher than it opened in that period
The period had no trading
The candle shows only the highest price

questions.q: Why should you choose a timeframe before looking at a chart?
options: To avoid switching timeframes until a pattern appears, which is hindsight
Because timeframes change the price
Because only daily charts are valid
Because charts cannot be read otherwise

questions.q: A chart shows higher highs and higher lows. What does this describe?
options: A guaranteed rise
An uptrend based on past prices
A sideways market
A certain future move

questions.q: Why is a support or resistance level better treated as a zone than as an exact line?
options: Because levels never matter
Because prices rarely stop at one exact number
Because zones are required by law
Because lines cannot be drawn on charts

questions.q: Price breaks above a resistance level. What is the most sensible response?
options: Buy at once because the level is broken
Review the view against rules written in advance before acting
Sell everything immediately
Assume the move will continue because it did once before

questions.q: A stop order sits below a buy price. The market opens far lower after a weekend event. What is the likely result?
options: The stop fills exactly at its level
The stop may fill at the first available price, which can be far below the stop
The stop cancels itself
The stop waits until Monday's close

questions.q: When is liquidity usually lowest?
options: During busy hours with many active traders
During quiet hours, around holidays and just before major events
Only at the market open
Only at the market close

questions.q: A scheduled economic release is due at ten o'clock. What is the most useful step before it?
options: Add to the position because the trend is strong
Decide in advance whether to trade it, and size the position so the worst fill is survivable
Ignore the calendar because scheduled news cannot move prices
Trade the first second of the release

questions.q: A headline appears on a market you hold. Which response follows good discipline?
options: Trade at once, because the first move shows the real direction
Check your plan, position size and maximum loss before deciding
Close every position in every market
Share the headline with friends before acting

questions.q: What is a gap in price?
options: A small change within one candle
A jump from one price level to the next with little or no trading between them
A fee charged by the broker
The difference between the bid and the ask
